intro.text: This is Karnataka, in the south of India. The sea is along its western edge. Then the land climbs into green hills, and behind the hills it opens out flat and wide and dry. Kerala is one of its neighbours. The main city is Bengaluru, which sits nearly a kilometre up in the air on top of that flat land.

animal.text: A giant squirrel lives in these trees and hardly ever comes down. He jumps from tree to tree. If something frightens him he goes flat against the trunk and keeps still.

food.text: Mysore pak is made of three things only: gram flour, butter and sugar, cooked together and cut into squares. The story goes that a cook made it up for a king.

festival.text: At Dasara an elephant walks through Mysore carrying a small golden house on its back. There is more gold in it than ten grown-ups weigh. A goddess rides inside.

hello.text: In Karnataka people say Namaskara. Kannada letters are all curves. That may be because they were once scratched on palm leaves, and a straight line would tear the leaf.

line.text: This is Mysore Palace. For nine nights every year, a hundred thousand little bulbs are lit all over this palace. Every arch, every dome and every edge of the roof turns into a line of gold, drawn on the dark.

A chariot stands in the courtyard of this temple, and all of it is stone: the wheels, the roof, the carvings. In front of it is a hall whose carved stone beams make a musical sound when they are struck, like bells nobody hung up.

This is Jog Falls. Here the river reaches a cliff and splits into four waterfalls side by side, and each one has a name. Raja comes down in one straight column. Roarer crashes into a cup of rock. Rani slides quietly in a sheet of foam. Rocket shoots out in jets.

This is Bandipur. A road runs through this forest, and wild elephants walk across it. So from nine at night until six in the morning nobody may drive along it. There is a gate at each end, and for those hours the road belongs to the animals.

Six small islands sit in the river here, and the trees on them are loaded with birds. Storks, pelicans and cormorants all nest in the same branches. You go round the islands in a rowing boat, and crocodiles lie about on the banks.
